doc.title: Scott Jimmy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Freddy Mendelsohn calls for Can't We Begin Again
summary: Mendelsohn offered a Savoy album and paid about $10,000, more than Lubinsky would have.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: You worked at old age homes. But then, in ’84, an interesting thing happens. Freddy Mendelsohn calls you. By now, Lubinsky’s gone. ’84. Jeannie Scott: ’74.

Yeah, oh, that’s what I meant to say: ’74. Lubinsky – Freddy Mendelsohn calls you in 1974, and he tells you he wants you to do an album – another album for Savoy, Can’t We Begin Again?, which has all sorts of hopeful implications. Tell me about that album. Jimmy Scott: I don’t know. I never saw any publicity on it, and I hardly heard it on the radio. That’s the way they worked.
But he gave you some money for that, didn’t he, or not?
Because I got the idea that he wanted to a degree [to] make up . . .
Which is a whole lot more than you ever got from . . .
Whole lot more than Lubinsky would have gave. The best I’d have got out of Lubinsky is $5,000.
